text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The share price of market leader Vilnius Bank reached a new 1,220 litas high during the stock exchange session Thursday.

- Experts from the elite French police unit R.A.I.D. provided theoretical and practical training to a Lithuanian rapid response unit, Aras. "They are well trained and there are things we could learn from them," commented one French expert.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas considers relations with neighbouring countries as the best in Lithuanian history and called relations with Poland "exemplary".
- Advertisement producers say it is more difficult to advertise politicians than soap or chocolate. The newspaper analyses the PR campaign of different political parties.
- 200 workers of an agricultural cooperative in the southwest Lithuanian region of Raseiniai stopped work yesterday afternoon and due to the lack of fodder 13,000 pigs went hungry.
- Corruption in the courts does not interest Lithuanian lawmakers: parliament lacked enough votes to strip immunity from two judges from the second city of Kaunas, alleged to have taken bribes.

- The government issued credit settlement guarantees Wednesday to Lucent Technologies, which used to be part of U.S. giant AT&T, for $3 million to modernise the communication system in the interior ministry. The credit has a 10-year maturity.
- Contraband alcohol accounts for nearly 60 percent of alcohol consumed in Lithuania.
- The right-wing opposition party Homeland Union (Conservatives) economy experts intend to start a general revision of remaining state-owned property if they win the parliament elections.

- Germany has invested more into the Lithuanian economy than any other state but the total investment volume is not big when compared to German investments in Poland, Hungary or Slovakia. The head of the economy department in the Lithuanian Embassy in Bonn Algimantas Kundrotas thinks that German businessman do not consider Lithuania a safe and reliable country.
